note: THE LEG RECORD'S SHAPE, AND THE TEXT THE MODEL IS SHOWN BEFORE IT
COMPOSES ONE (kogaki#1108).
WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, stated first because it is what separates it from
every other schema carrier in src/. The other schemas are read by a
validator and by nothing else: they describe a record the composing party
already knows the shape of. This one is read TWICE, and the second reader
is the point. `validateLegs` in src/compose.mjs reads the field set from
it, and the path-composition state of the Brief workflow table RENDERS it
into the judge's prompt. So the text the Model composes against and the
text the refusal enforces are one file and cannot disagree.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, measured on 2026-09-12 over the two live Briefs
(theses/calling-saved-permission-durable-leaves and
theses/legs-real-quality-matter-degree). No file declared the Leg's
fields or what they mean. The composer inferred the shape from
.claude/skills/brief/SKILL.md's prose, wrote a Candidates JSON, and
`validateLegs` checked it afterwards -- so the only Harness text carrying
what a field means was a refusal string, seen only when shape had already
failed. Claim cardinality drifted accordingly: the first Brief carried 1
to 3 claims per Leg, the second 4 to 6, with up to six claims from one
Strand in a single Leg.
IT CARRIES THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH TOO (kogaki#1147). The field
table below is about one Leg; `path_rules` is about the sequence -- the
Section grouping, the order `depends_on` may name, the uniqueness of an id,
the claim cardinality. Those were enforced in src/compose.mjs and stated
nowhere a composer reads, so a path satisfied them by chance or learned
them from a refusal that had already spent an attempt. The refusals now
read their text from that section, for the reason the field set is read
from this one.
IT DECLARES SHAPE AND MEANING, AND JUDGES NEITHER. Every MUST of the
composition design stays judgment-class and is judged at path review. A
missing field is refused here; a weak rationale is not, and no description
below is ever matched against a value.
SPEC REFERENCES IN THIS FILE (kogaki#902; one carrier, kogaki#982).
The rule these entries are written under -- what a copy is, what the two
markers `[implemented-against: ...]` and `[see: ...]` mean, and why nothing
names a section number or a line range -- lives in ONE place:
`src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`. It is not restated here.

what_a_leg_is: A Leg is one move of the Reader Path: the smallest unit that takes the
reader from one state to another. `Leg = Input + State` -- the Input is
the material it stands on (its Strands), and the State is the Move it
binds, which is what names the kind of reader-state transition it makes.
A Leg that no Move in the library fits says so in `no_move_fits` instead
of naming the nearest Move, and its Candidate is refused with that sentence.

The Leg's shape is the field table below. A Leg carries exactly one of `move` and `no_move_fits`: a Leg no Move fits says so, and its Candidate is refused with that sentence rather than adopted (kogaki#1276).

leg_id.description: This Leg's own id, unique within the path. Other Legs address it through `depends_on`, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id.

materials.description: The Strands this Leg stands on, as LessonDisplayIDs (`L<n>`). A Leg with no material asserts nothing on anyone's behalf.

purpose.description: What this Leg is for in the path -- the work it does toward the adopted Thesis, in one or two sentences. A VERB ABOUT THE READER, carrying no proposition from the material: a purpose that could be true or false of the world is a claim in the wrong field.

reader_state_before.description: What the reader holds when this Leg begins, in the Move library's own dimensions (knowledge, question, expectation, orientation, trust -- the Move library entry) -- one `dimension: value` LINE per dimension the Leg's Move addresses. This is a line-per-dimension shape, not the bound Move's own `before` shape verbatim -- a Move's `before` folds its dimensions into one paragraph, and a dimension's value there is ordinary prose free to carry any punctuation (kogaki#1211). Judged at the specialization occasion against the Move's `before`: a Leg's before-state must be a consistent specialization of what its Move demands. ON THE FIRST LEG the comparison state is the Brief's READER START instead of the Move's `before` (kogaki#1216): Reader start is a cold read authored from the Persona and the Thesis, never from the Move this Leg binds, and this field is judged against it on the same terms every other Leg is judged against its Move -- `specializes` passes, `contradicts` refuses. No verbatim match remains; see `first_leg_binds_a_survivor` below for the rule that governs which Move the first Leg may bind.

reader_state_after.description: What the reader holds when this Leg ends, in the same dimensions and the same line-per-dimension shape as `reader_state_before`. Judged against the Move's `after` the same way. The two state fields are the Leg's transition, written as the reader's condition rather than as the writer's intent -- the reader's CONDITION afterwards, never a proposition about the world. ON THE LEG MARKED `reaches_target` this field IS the Brief's Reader target (kogaki#1231, owner decision 2026-09-30, reversing kogaki#1225's last-Leg derivation): the Brief renders that Leg's after-state, whole and line for line, under its `Reader target` heading, and no separate field authors it -- a Candidate carrying `reader_target` is refused by name. No Opening question is rendered any more and the first Leg's after-state owes no `question:` line: whatever question the opening leaves the reader holding belongs here, in the reader's own words, and nowhere else.

reaches_target.description: Present, and true, on exactly ONE Leg of the path -- never the first (kogaki#1231, owner decision 2026-09-30, reversing kogaki#1225's rule that the Reader target sits wherever the path ends). That Leg's `reader_state_after` IS the Brief's Reader target, and its `leg_id` is what the Thesis Closure row's `established_by_legs` names. Every Leg AFTER the marked one is a CLOSING Leg, held to the three closing-Leg path_rules below: it introduces nothing, raises no Closure row, and its `orientation` and `knowledge` lines hold at the marked Leg's -- only `question`, `expectation` and `trust` may still move. A Leg before the marked one carries no meaning from this field at all; the marking is absent.

names.description: Present on the Leg marked `reaches_target`, and there alone: the terms this path's own `introduces` entries have put in the reader's hands by the time `reader_state_after` -- the Brief's Reader target -- is reached. It is a LIST, not prose, because the Reader target heading renders `reader_state_after` whole and line for line and cannot itself enumerate what the reader now knows by name. A Leg before the mark, or a closing Leg after it, carries no meaning from this field at all; the marking is absent.

depends_on.description: The EARLIER Legs whose conclusions this Leg stands on, by `leg_id`. May be empty. An id that is not an earlier Leg is refused -- a dependency on a later Leg is a path that cannot be read in order. The ordering rule is a property of the whole path and is stated in `path_rules` below.

rationale.description: Why this Leg sits HERE, at this position, rather than earlier or later. The ORDER ARGUMENT, not a restatement of the purpose and not a claim the Leg asserts.

move.description: The Move library entry this Leg binds, by id. The Move IS the State component of a Leg. COMPOSE IT FROM `moves_you_may_bind` IN THIS ASK'S INPUT AND FROM NOTHING ELSE: that field carries every admitted Move with its `before`, `after`, `technique` and `breaks`, read from the Move file. `before` and `after` are the reader states the Move moves between; `technique` is the general route between them, which this Leg SPECIALIZES in its own `waypoints`; `breaks` are the tests that route must survive. Choose a Move only where you can write waypoints that specialize its `technique` from this Leg's own claims and materials and that survive each `breaks` test. THE MOVE IS READ HERE AND NEVER AGAIN (kogaki#1311, owner decision 2026-10-09): no stage after the Candidate opens a Move, so the writer meets this Leg's waypoints and never the Move's prose. An id outside the set resolves to no record and is refused at composition, naming the Leg and the id. A Leg carries exactly one of `move` and `no_move_fits` (kogaki#1125, kogaki#1276).

no_move_fits.description: Present ONLY where no Move in `moves_you_may_bind` fits this Leg: one sentence naming what this Leg's claims need that no Move's `technique` provides. Never name the nearest Move instead. A Leg carries exactly one of `move` and `no_move_fits`, and a Candidate with any `no_move_fits` Leg is refused with that sentence, so the next attempt can revise the path: omit the Leg, change the path, or leave a Strand unused (kogaki#1276).

claims.description: What this Leg ASSERTS, one entry per Strand it names in `materials`. A claim is a PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD and names no reader; a claim that mentions the reader belongs in `purpose` or in a state field. Its ground is the pinned Lesson, held as an address in the Brief's Strands section and never copied here. A claim is stated in EVERYDAY WORDS plus the words the Persona's `prior_knowledge` grants (owner decision 2026-10-06): where the Strand's own vocabulary and the Persona's do not match, the claim conforms to the Persona, never to the Strand's term of art. Any other word appears in a claim only if an `introduces` entry on this Leg or an earlier Leg carries it -- the reader-knowledge ledger is what makes a term available to speak of. An absent or empty `prior_knowledge` grants no extra word and refuses nothing: the Persona may be empty or very general, and the design does not fail when it grants nothing. See `claim` below -- the cardinality rule is the part most likely to be got wrong.

waypoints.description: The route this Leg takes the reader along, from `reader_state_before` to `reader_state_after`, as an ORDERED list of waypoints -- this Leg's specialization of its Move's `technique` (kogaki#1311, owner decision 2026-10-09). Each waypoint is a POINT: the proposition its paragraph makes, in the article's subject, one sentence (kogaki#1326, owner decision 2026-10-10) -- what the paragraph establishes, never how the reader is to feel or what they are handed, and never a stage direction. The point is not quoted; its wording is the writer's. Each names the claim or claims of this Leg it serves, and every claim of this Leg is served by at least one waypoint. How many waypoints a Leg carries is yours to decide from the Move's prose and this Leg's claims: you need not reproduce the Move's internal structure element for element, even where its `technique` describes a fixed number, and nothing reads the count. One waypoint tends to become one paragraph, as a strong tendency rather than a guarantee. A waypoint whose point no claim of this Leg supports is the signal that the Leg is short of material: pull in a Journey, bind another Move, or report `no_move_fits` -- never a waypoint serving a claim it does not draw on. See `waypoint` below.

journeys.description: The Journeys this Leg draws on, each naming the Strand whose Journey it takes and what the Leg uses it for. A Journey is MATERIAL THE LEG EDITS, never an assertion the Leg must recover -- it carries no claim, Reverse Outlining checks no fragment of it, and the Leg Packet renders it as prose to edit for this Leg's waypoints. Nothing here bounds how many a Leg declares: a Leg telling two cases for one claim is a path-review judgment, the way the number of claims is bounded by the Leg's materials rather than by a number. See `journey` below.

entailed.description: True where a proposition this Leg asserts is not explicit in the material and is reached by inference. The flag is the composer's judgment; the Harness refuses only a flag with no reasoning beside it.

entailment_reasoning.description: The inference itself, stated so path review and the owner can judge it. Entailment is interpretation, judged rather than silently trusted.

bridges.description: Present only on a Leg inserted between two adjacent Legs to repair a causal gap between them; names that adjacent pair by `leg_id`. It is disclosed at the Candidate-selection gate, so an unvalidated marking would render at an owner surface. The Bridge Leg is where that insertion is defined.

introduces.description: Terms this Leg introduces to the reader for the first time, one item per term. The accumulated ledger the Leg Packet renders is derived from these; whether a term is genuinely new HERE is a judgment and is not checked. The reader-knowledge ledger is the accumulation this feeds. See `introduces_item` below -- its `term` field is what `re-activate`'s `term` form and the introduced-term refusal both match against.

re-activate.description: What this Leg treats as active material, restored from a Leg it depends on — not an inventory of what the reader possesses, but what the Writer may speak of as this Leg's own. One reference per line, in one of THREE forms: `<leg_id> term <exact introduces term>` (the string must match, verbatim, the `term` of an entry in that Leg's `introduces`), `<leg_id> claim <strand id> as <one plain sentence>` (the strand must be one that Leg carries a claim for, and the `as` sentence is required -- a plain restatement of that claim written at Brief time, never the claim's own `proposition` rendered verbatim), or `<leg_id> journey <strand id>` (the strand must be one that Leg names in its `journeys`). The named Leg must be in this Leg's `depends_on`. Anything not named here stays available to the reader but is not material for this Leg to speak of; the composer selects from what `depends_on` makes reachable and writes no free text here beyond the `as` sentence the claim form requires.

opens_section.description: Present on a Leg that opens a Section of the finished article; carries that Section's name. The four grouping rules are a property of the WHOLE PATH and run after every Leg is known to be well formed -- they are stated in `path_rules` below, as the validator checks them, and three of the four refuse. The Section grouping carries the four rules.

figure.description: The composer's statement of what a figure lets the reader hold here that the prose leaves hard to hold. The default is NO figure: a Leg without this field has none and nothing asks about it. The figure decision is where the field is defined.

figure_roles.description: Binds every role of the Move's `figure` to one of THIS Leg's own claims, addressed `g<n>` and numbered from 1 in the order the claims are declared. A role bound to another Leg's claim is unreachable by construction: the address space is this Leg's claims and has no syntax for anyone else's.

budget.description: The word bound this Leg's realized prose may spend, rendered in the Packet's write instruction. A LIMIT THE WRITER SEES, never a target to reach -- its absence means no bound is declared, and nothing asks about it.

note: THE RULES OVER THE WHOLE PATH, AND WHY THEY ARE DECLARED HERE
(kogaki#1147). Everything above is a rule about ONE Leg, and a composer
was already shown it. The rules below are about the PATH -- a Leg's
relation to its neighbours, and the sequence taken as a whole -- and until
this issue they lived in code alone: `validateLegs` and
`sectionGroupingRefusal` in src/compose.mjs raised them, and the composing
party met one for the first time in a refusal that had already cost one of
its three attempts. Two runs on 2026-09-18 died at path composition on the
Section grouping's rule 4, each having satisfied every field-level rule it
was shown. A rule enforced over a record and never stated to the party
that composes it can be satisfied only by chance.
THE REFUSALS READ THEIR TEXT FROM THE ENTRIES BELOW, which is the same
arrangement the field table above already has: the prompt and the refusal
cannot disagree when there is one file. A rule stated here with no refusal
reading it, or a refusal composing its own wording, is the two-carrier
drift this file exists to remove -- and `checks/check-brief-compose.sh`
reads every refusal these two functions raise back against this section.
EACH ENTRY CARRIES `name` AND `rule`. The `name` is what the refusal says
first, so a refused composer can find the rule it broke by searching this
file for the words it was just handed; the `rule` is the rule as the
validator checks it. `class` is `checked` where a refusal enforces it and
`judgment` where it is yours to make -- a judgment-class rule is stated
HERE, beside the checked ones, because the two read alike to whoever
composes against them and only one of them will ever refuse. Nothing
below is matched against a value: a rule marked `judgment` is judged at
path review, and Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint is the
rule that keeps it there.
The Section grouping is where the four Section rules are ratified; the
Leg's shape carries the path's own order and the uniqueness of an id; the
claims rule carries the cardinality.

path_is_non_empty.name: the Leg's shape -- a path is an ordered sequence of Legs
path_is_non_empty.rule: A composed path is a NON-EMPTY, ORDERED array of Leg records, read in the order it is written.

leg_id_unique.name: the Leg's shape -- one id per Leg
leg_id_unique.rule: Each `leg_id` is unique within the path. Two Legs sharing an id leave every `depends_on` naming it ambiguous, and the specialization record carries one verdict per id, so it would address both at once.

depends_on_ordering.name: the Leg's shape -- depends_on names an EARLIER Leg
depends_on_ordering.rule: Every id in a Leg's `depends_on` names a Leg EARLIER in the path. An id that is not an earlier Leg -- a later one, or one no Leg carries -- is a path that cannot be read in order.

one_claim_per_strand.name: the claims rule -- one claim per Strand, per Leg
one_claim_per_strand.rule: A Leg asserts ONE claim on behalf of each Strand it names in `materials`. A Strand that serves several Legs carries a DIFFERENT claim in each -- that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement -- so the repair for a second claim is to move it to the Leg where the reader needs it, or to drop it, never to merge the two into a longer proposition.

section_rule_1.name: the Section grouping rule 1
section_rule_1.rule: A Leg OPENS a Section when it changes the reader's question -- its `purpose` answers a question the previous Leg did not pose, or its `introduces` names a term later Legs use. This is the positive case and it is YOURS TO JUDGE: nothing checks it, and its violation is exactly rule 2's refusal.

section_rule_2.name: the Section grouping rule 2
section_rule_2.rule: A Leg CONTINUES the current Section when it develops the previous one -- when its `depends_on` is exactly the immediately preceding Leg AND its `materials` overlap that Leg's. A Leg that develops its predecessor may not open a new Section.

section_rule_3.name: the Section grouping rule 3
section_rule_3.rule: The FIRST Leg of the path always opens a Section. A path that declares `opens_section` nowhere renders as one unbroken run of prose, which is the second of the two drafts the 2026-09-03 ruling rejected.

section_rule_4.name: the Section grouping rule 4
section_rule_4.rule: TWO ADJACENT SECTIONS HOLDING EXACTLY ONE LEG EACH are refused with a request to MERGE them, because a heading on every Leg is the first of the two drafts the ruling rejected. Length enters as a bound on the grouping, never as its reason.
section_rule_4.the_other_clause: Rule 4's other clause -- a Section running past roughly a display and a half of prose without a heading -- measures REALIZED PROSE, which no Brief contains. It is a named deferred slot in the Section grouping: it binds your judgment while you group the Legs, and no refusal reads it.

reaches_target_marked.name: the Reader target Leg -- exactly one Leg marked, and never the first
reaches_target_marked.rule: EXACTLY ONE Leg of the path carries `reaches_target: true`, and it is not the first Leg. Zero marked Legs leaves the Brief's Reader target undecided; two or more leaves it ambiguous which after-state is the target; marking the first Leg leaves no Leg free to reach it from anywhere (kogaki#1231).

closing_leg_introduces_nothing.name: the Reader target Leg -- a closing Leg introduces nothing and raises nothing
closing_leg_introduces_nothing.rule: A Leg AFTER the one marked `reaches_target` is a CLOSING Leg. A closing Leg carries no `introduces` entry, and it is named as `introduced_by` on no Closure row: once the Reader target is reached, nothing new is put in front of the reader and no new promise is raised for a later Leg to keep (kogaki#1231).

closing_leg_state_fixed.name: the Reader target Leg -- a closing Leg's orientation and knowledge hold at the target Leg's
closing_leg_state_fixed.rule: A closing Leg's `reader_state_after` carries the SAME `orientation` and `knowledge` lines, line for line, as the Leg marked `reaches_target` -- once the reader arrives, a closing Leg may not move them further in either dimension. Its `question`, `expectation` and `trust` lines are free to differ (kogaki#1231).

closure_one_conceded_row.name: Closure -- at most one conceded row in the path
closure_one_conceded_row.rule: A path carries AT MOST ONE Closure row whose terminal state is `conceded_by`. A Question a Leg will not close is set aside IN THAT LEG rather than carried forward (owner decision 2026-09-30): a row's `conceded_by` may name the same Leg as its `introduced_by`, and that is the ordinary case, not an exception. Two or three rows needing to be set aside is read as a sign the ReaderPath itself is not suitable, so a second `conceded_by` row is refused rather than rendered -- the repair is to close the row where it is raised, or to reshape the path. A conceded row carries three further fields, required only there and declared beside the row's other fields in `src/candidate-schema.json`'s `obligations`: `open` (what stays unresolved), `why_not_here` (why this Leg is not the one to close it) and `reader_keeps` (what the reader is left holding in its place).

closure_one_row_open_per_leg.name: Closure -- at most one row open at any given Leg
closure_one_row_open_per_leg.rule: A Closure row is OPEN on every Leg from its `introduced_by` Leg up to, and NOT INCLUDING, the Leg that closes it (`discharged_by` or `conceded_by`); a row raised and closed in the same Leg is open on no Leg. AT MOST ONE non-Thesis row may be open at any given Leg (owner decision 2026-09-30): the Thesis is carried throughout by design, but a Question or a promise is a milestone on the way to closing it, and two of them held open at once is the Brief bringing more than one loose end to the same stretch of the reader's attention. A Leg on which more than one row is open is refused, naming the Leg and every row open there.

first_leg_binds_a_survivor.name: the first Leg binds a Move that does not contradict Reader start
first_leg_binds_a_survivor.rule: The FIRST Leg opens from the Brief's READER START -- a cold read authored from the Persona and the Thesis at the `differentiation` state, never from any Move (kogaki#1216, owner decision 2026-09-28). Which Move it may bind is decided by EXCLUSION, NOT OPTIMIZATION: a Move is excluded when its `before` contradicts Reader start on a dimension it declares; a Move that omits a dimension is not excluded on it. The survivors are listed on the differentiation record as `leg1_survivors` and are NOT RANKED -- no score exists anywhere -- and your assigned `opening_move` is one of them. You bind it by the SAME composition order every Leg uses (Strand information, then Leg reasoning, then the Move), and the grounds test applies: delete the Move name from the first Leg's `rationale`, and what remains must still stand on its grounds. Your first Leg's `reader_state_before` is then judged at the specialization occasion against Reader start in place of its Move's `before` -- `specializes` passes, `contradicts` refuses. Reader start is the state of a reader who has seen the Thesis as a title and nothing else (kogaki#1225), so ONE refusal is deterministic: a Reader start line containing a term ANY Leg of this path lists under `introduces:` is refused at adoption naming the term and the Leg -- a term the path introduces is by definition one the reader does not hold on arrival. The Brief records how many Moves survived; a count of one names the library, not this rule, as the cause of a repeated opening.

retired.reader_start_binds_first_leg: a `checked` rule that refused the first Leg's `reader_state_before` on anything but a VERBATIM match with Reader start. With the specialization rule beside it, it forced Reader start to be written backwards from the first Leg's Move -- the Move's `before` with the article's nouns substituted -- which is the defect kogaki#1216 removes. No verbatim match remains anywhere.

definition: A CLAIM IS THE ONE PROPOSITION THIS LEG ASSERTS ON BEHALF OF ONE
STRAND, FOR THIS READER AT THIS POINT IN THE PATH.
ITS GROUND IS THE PINNED LESSON, HELD AS AN ADDRESS AND NEVER COPIED.
In Toulmin's layout the claim is what is asserted and the ground is the
data it rests on; this field carries the assertion, and the Lesson it
rests on stays at its pin in the Brief's Strands section. The Lesson's
own Claim sentence is at that pin and is never rendered here or in the
Leg Packet, which is what keeps `assert nothing beyond` checkable:
what the Leg may assert is this list, and nothing arrives beside it.
A CLAIM IS A PROPOSITION ABOUT THE WORLD AND NAMES NO READER. The
boundary against the Leg's other fields is one of grammatical kind:
`purpose` is a verb about the reader and carries no proposition from
the material, `reader_state_after` is the reader's condition
afterwards, and `rationale` is the order argument. A claim that
mentions the reader, or a purpose that could be true or false of the
world, is in the wrong field.
ONE CLAIM PER STRAND NAMED IN `materials`. Two claims in one Leg
naming the same Strand is REFUSED, naming the Leg and the Strand. A
Strand that serves several Legs carries a DIFFERENT claim in each --
that is what makes the path a sequence rather than a restatement, and it
is why the rule is per Leg rather than per path.
WHY THE CARDINALITY IS BOUNDED AT ALL, measured rather than argued
(kogaki#1108). The Leg Packet requires every declared claim to be
recoverable from the realized passage, and `claims` fails the
Leg otherwise. With cardinality unbounded, claim generation drifted
into composing the article's decisive lines wholesale and calling them
claims -- so the comparison the Packet performs stopped measuring
grounding and started measuring how much of the passage had been written
in advance. One proposition per Strand is what keeps a claim a claim
the Strand supports rather than a draft of the sentence that will carry
it.
A CLAIM IS ONE PROPOSITION DERIVED FROM A STRAND, AND NOTHING ELSE. The
type set is closed at `strand`. Inherited reader state belongs to
`reader_state_before` and to the computed `already knows` ledger; a
presupposed premise belongs to the Brief's Reader start. Neither is an
assertion, so a passage that realizes its Leg correctly never states
one and the Blind Reader never recovers it.
The claims rule is the spec half of this definition; the mechanical half -- the closed type set and the one-per-Strand refusal -- is carried here and enforced by `validateLegs`.

retired_types.leg_effect: inherited reader state, which is already carried by this Leg's `reader_state_before` and by the computed `already knows` ledger
retired_types.reader_assumption: a presupposed premise, which belongs to the Brief's Reader start

type.description: The closed set above. Today it has one member, `strand`.

proposition.description: The claim itself, STATED -- a specific proposition this Leg asserts, not a pointer at where one could be found. An untyped pointer is not a claim.

strand.description: The Strand this claim is asserted on behalf of, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Leg's `materials`, it is where the pinned Lesson that grounds the claim is addressed, and no other claim of this Leg names it.

definition: A WAYPOINT IS A POINT ITS PARAGRAPH MAKES (kogaki#1326, owner decision
2026-10-10, replacing the effect form kogaki#1311 introduced). The
Leg's `reader_state_before` and `reader_state_after` say where the
reader starts and ends; the waypoints say, in order, what the Leg's
paragraphs establish to get them from one to the other. The Move's
`technique` says that in general and for every article; a Leg's
waypoints say it for THIS Leg's claims, in the article's subject.
A POINT, NEVER AN EFFECT AND NEVER A SENTENCE TO COPY. `point` is the
proposition the paragraph makes, in one sentence. It names what the
paragraph establishes -- never how the reader is to feel, what they
are "handed", or when they "receive" something: an effect is a
stage direction, and a writer given one narrates it. Nor is it the
Move's technique with the subject filled in. The point is not quoted:
its wording is the writer's.
IT SERVES A CLAIM. A point need not restate the claim; it is a
proposition obtainable from the claim it serves. A reinforcing step --
an example, a consequence, an answer to the obvious objection -- names
the claim it reinforces in `serves`.
THE MOVE'S RESPONSIBILITY ENDS HERE. The Move is read when the Leg is
composed and judged, and never again: the Leg Packet renders these
waypoints in place of any Move field, and nothing after the Candidate
opens a Move file. So whatever the writer needs from the Move has to be
in the waypoints.
WHAT IS REFUSED IS SHAPE, AND THE COUNT IS NOT. `validateLegs` refuses
an empty list, a waypoint with an empty `point` or an empty `serves`,
a waypoint carrying the retired `effect`, a `serves` entry naming a
Strand this Leg carries no claim for, and a
claim of this Leg that no waypoint serves -- each naming the Leg and
the waypoint. Whether the waypoints specialize the Move's `technique`
and survive its `breaks` is judged, at the Move-fit judgment, and never
a lint.

point.description: The proposition this paragraph makes, in the article's subject, in one sentence -- what the paragraph establishes. Never how the reader is to feel or what they are handed, and never a sentence for the writer to copy: its wording is the writer's.

serves.description: The claim or claims of this Leg this step serves, each named by the Strand id its claim names (`L<n>`). Every entry is a Strand this Leg carries a claim for.

definition: A JOURNEY IS MATERIAL THE LEG DRAWS ON, NEVER AN ASSERTION THE LEG
MUST RECOVER. A Lesson's Claim is a proposition, and the planning
decision is what transformation of it this Leg asserts -- so it is
carried in the Brief as the Leg's claim. A Journey is a Strand that
supplies a concrete example, and how much of it a Leg draws on depends
on the Move being performed and on the prose already on the page -- so
it is ADDRESSED at planning and EDITED at realization. That asymmetry is
the whole of why this field carries an address and a use rather than any
text. It is not fundamentally different from a Claim -- apart from
allowing more detailed specification, it is a long Strand that CAN be
turned into a narrative, but is never rendered as one merely because it
is called a Journey; its purpose is to supply technically appropriate,
relevant concrete examples, and it is not evidence (kogaki#1323, owner
THE BRIEF CARRIES NO JOURNEY TEXT. The entry names a Strand and what
this Leg uses that Strand's Journey for; the prose lives at the
Strand's served journey cite, which the Brief already renders in its
Strands section. No decomposition of a Journey happens at planning
time.
IT ASSERTS NOTHING, AND THE CONSEQUENCES ARE MECHANICAL. A Journey
generates no claim, so `claims` never asks for it back and the
Reverse Outline the Blind Reader hands over carries no Journey field
to compare. What this Leg may ASSERT is its `claims` list, and a
Journey placed here does not widen it.
THE USE IS FROM A CLOSED SET, in plain words, read from `uses` below.
It is what the Leg does with the material, not a claim about the
world: a use outside the set is refused by `validateLegs`, and
whether the use chosen serves the Move is path review's judgment.
COVERAGE ACCOUNTING IS TAKEN FROM THIS FIELD. Journey placement is
counted from `journeys`: a Strand's Journey is placed by a Leg when
that Leg declares an entry naming it here. It was once counted from a
`<L-id>.journey` token in `materials` instead, and that made two
readers of one fact -- a Leg that named its Strand bare and drew on
its Journey here rendered its `journey:` line and was disclosed as
OMITTED in the same Brief. A `<L-id>.journey` token stays legal, and
still names the Strand; it no longer places anything on its own.
`use` IS READ BY `validateLegs`, THE BRIEF AND COVERAGE ACCOUNTING, AND
BY NOTHING IN THE PACKET (kogaki#1286, owner decision 2026-10-06). The
Brief renders it with this section's gloss, resolved there; the Packet's
Journey block renders the Strand's served text and its cite under the
block's existing header, and none of the three use words.

uses.illustrate: to illustrate this Leg's claim with the case that illustrates it
uses.motivate: to motivate the question this Leg opens, with the case that motivates it
uses.contrast: to contrast this Leg's claim with the case that contrasts it

strand.description: The Strand whose Journey this Leg draws on, as a LessonDisplayID (`L<n>`). It is one of this Leg's `materials` -- named bare or as `<L-id>.journey` -- and its served record must carry Journey material, which is what the Brief's `- journey cite:` line records.

use.description: What this Leg uses the Journey for, from the closed set in `uses` above. A use outside that set is refused.

definition: ONE TERM A LEG INTRODUCES, TYPED BY WHERE IT CAME FROM. A term new to
the reader is new for one of two reasons -- this Leg is coining it, or
this Leg is the first to bring in a term that already has a home
outside the article -- and the two carry different obligations to the
reader, so `kind` is required rather than left to prose.

term.description: The term itself, exactly as it must appear to match -- `re-activate`'s `term` form and the introduced-term refusal both match this string verbatim.

kind.description: `coined` -- this Leg names something for the first time anywhere, inventing the term. `established` -- the term already has a home outside this article, and this Leg is the first to bring it in here.

meaning.description: One sentence giving the term's meaning. Required on a `coined` term, because nothing outside this Leg can supply it. On an `established` term, `source` stands as the meaning and this field is not asked for separately -- the term crosses into a later Leg's Packet carrying whichever of the two it has.

source.description: Where an established term comes from -- the field, the text or the person it is established by. A coined term has no source but this Leg, so the field is absent there. Stands as the term's meaning when it crosses into a later Leg's Packet.

nearest.description: For a coined term, the nearest existing term a reader might reach for instead. Optional even on a coined term -- some coinages have no near neighbour worth naming. At most one introduces item across the whole path may carry `nearest` -- a second one is refused.

differs.description: For a coined term, how it differs from `nearest` -- why the nearest existing term will not do. Present only beside `nearest`; a `differs` with no `nearest` names nothing to differ from.

what_is_judged_elsewhere: Nothing here is a lint over a judgment. Whether a rationale is good,
whether a claim is genuinely supported by its Strand, whether a term is
really introduced here, and whether the before/after states are faithful
specializations of the Move are all judgment-class: they are judged at
path review and at the specialization occasion, and a refusal from this
Every MUST is judgment, and nothing becomes a lint -- which is the rule this paragraph is an instance of.
